issues.claim: CATALOGUE-GAP (C-wall-raised). A primary that S5b spawns, crossing its own stage's boundary on its own viaduct, leaves the stage one gate short of N_k. §4.4 S5b (base l.5907-5918) opens 'The stage's primaries match its gates: N_k = the gate law'. It counts the existing arterials' crossings c 'on ground part 0 (a crossing on a raised deck no gate, S5a Trace (2))'. When N_k > c it spawns N_k - c radials, 'routes each with the incremental S4 router ... and may raise a viaduct by §4.3's rules. The crossings become stage k's main gates.' §4.3 The slot places 'a viaduct ... each later stage's S5b through this router'. S5a Trace (2) pins no gate where 'an arterial crossing the boundary on a raised deck' meets it (l.5856-5857). §2.7's support step (6) (d) makes the stage's ring a stretch laid after that viaduct: 'it takes no crossing station and makes no gate on the deck'. So when a spawned radial raises its viaduct across the valley at its own boundary, the stage gets N_k - 1 gates, and 'primaries match its gates' and §4.8's 'Gates - exactly N, by construction' (l.7655) fail. S5b spawns once and never recounts its own primaries, and no rung or report covers the shortfall. The case is a tested path: T110-2 (2) runs 'a stage-2 S5b viaduct crossed by stage 2's own moated ring' (l.18485-18486), and stage 2's S5b viaducts are its spawned primaries. Its bar checks the ring beneath the deck but no gate count. S5b's own test ('each epoch stage whose N_k exceeds its crossings adds >= 1 primary') passes with the shortfall, and §5.3's counts pass too ('so counted'). So one builder ships N_k - 1 gates, while another spawns a replacement or keeps the viaduct off the boundary. This is new with R5-02: under R4-09 the crossing was a raised gate.
issues.required_change: §4.4 S5b, after 'and may raise a viaduct by §4.3's rules.', add: 'Its own primaries' crossings are counted as c is, on ground part 0: for each spawned primary whose course crosses the boundary on a raised deck, ramp or stair (its viaduct's, which the trace runs on beneath; S5a Trace (2); §2.7's support step (6) (d)), S5b spawns one more by the same nested picks in the same batch, until the stage's crossings on ground part 0 reach N_k or no approachable gap remains - the shortfall then raised and reported as a request below the law is.' S5b's Test adds 'a stage whose spawned primary is raised across its own boundary still has N_k gates on ground part 0'. §4.8 Gates: 'each outer enceinte's gates are its S5b primaries' crossings' -> 'each outer enceinte's gates are its S5b primaries' crossings on ground part 0 (§4.4 S5b)'. End at scope: §13.2 T110-2 (2), after 'a stage-2 S5b viaduct crossed by stage 2's own moated ring', add '- stage 2's gates N_k, each on ground part 0, the viaduct's deck crossing none and one more primary spawned for it'.

issues.claim: CATALOGUE-GAP (C-wall-raised x C-raised-history). A wall run laid after a raised way, when a part it was built against goes. §2.7's support step (6) (d) (base l.2603-2616) builds a later wall run against the raised way. 'each part of the reservation standing in its band is taken into the line, the run abutting its faces and closed against it'; 'at a vault span ending at its arch vault's two walled-up arch mouths, the chamber kept whole'; and 'beneath every other span ... an ordinary run whose top is no higher than that span's soffit (... derived at read ...)'. Its readers say the same: V06 §3.7.6 (5), T110-2 (4), V07 §3.5a (4), §8.4 (l.13672-13673, l.13897-13898) and §11.1's glTF and CityJSON rows (l.15988-15989), 'a run beneath a raised way's span topped at its soffit'. Nothing states what the run is once those parts go, and every one of them can go after the run is laid. V06 §3.19.2 (3) dismantles a support whose spans have fallen, leaving it cleared (V06 l.2925-2931); only a crossing station is spared, and a support a later wall abuts is no station. (4)'s topple takes a support. A vault span's breach collapses its arch-vault chamber 'in the same batch' (l.2932-2934), and that chamber was the part 'closing the line' between the run's two ends. A span falls ruined or cleared, so its soffit no longer exists, though §8.4 and §11.1 still cap the run at 'a raised way's span'. A hand delete of the raised way removes its vaults in the same commit (T-V4-63). So the wall line is left with a gap - a pier's width, or a whole span's length where a vault stood - or with a run capped under a deck that no longer exists. One builder leaves a gap in the enceinte (its barrier closure broken with no breach recorded); another closes it; another keeps the cap. The path is normal in long histories: H-AQUA's epoch circuit runs beneath its standing aqueduct (T-V6-47), and an aqueduct that runs dry lapses, falls by span and is salvaged (V06 §3.19.2 (2)-(3)). V07 defines the village case only at the next derivation (T-V7-48). No bar runs the town case.
issues.required_change: §2.7's support step (6) (d), after '...`bend.wall.raisedCrossing`'s line at a hand edit's dry run).', add: 'What such a run is built against is read from the reservation as it stands - a support whose state is absent or ruined, a ramp, stair or foot of a standing raised way, a vault span whose state is absent with its arch vault - and its soffit cap from a span whose state is absent, both derived at read, never stored: where a part goes after the run was laid - a support cleared (V06 §3.19.2 (3)) or toppled (V06 §3.19.2 (4)), a vault span breached and its chamber collapsed with it, a span ruined or cleared, the raised way deleted or suppressed - the run stands whole across that part's former footprint and to its full height beneath the fallen span, in its own condition and material (its trace never left its course), with no gap and no op; its setback, glacis and berm stay as S7 cut them until the run is next re-traced (§7.3's S7 row).' (The adjudicator may instead rule the former footprint a breached run, provided the op removing the part is named as its one writer and the same bar runs it.) Ends: (1) rendering: §8.4's casters and heightfield and §11.1's glTF and CityJSON rows, 'a run beneath a raised way's span topped at its soffit' -> 'a run beneath a raised way's standing span (its state absent) topped at its soffit'. (2) V06: §3.19.2 (3)'s support and span bullets and (4)'s topple add 'a wall run laid after the way and built against what falls standing whole across its footprint (§2.7's support step (6) (d))'. (3) scope: §13.2 T110-2 (4) adds 'and, after its epoch circuit ran beneath the standing aqueduct, that aqueduct lapsed - its vault span in the band breached (its chamber collapsing) and a support in the band cleared by V06 §3.19.2 (3) - and, on a second run, the aqueduct deleted by hand: the run whole across each former support and the former vault, at full height beneath each fallen span, the enceinte's closure unchanged and 0 gaps in its band, the delete's undo restoring the abutments and the cap'.

issues.claim: CATALOGUE-GAP (C-wall-raised x C-raised-epoch). A raised way created across a run that is already breached or dismantled. Since R5-02 a crossing station is made only 'where a raised way is created across a standing wall'. Its support 'is the band's stretch under the deck', and it 'carries no state of its own - it reads its stretch's condition, ... breached or dismantled a ruined one' (§2.7's support step (3), base l.2548-2575). The only rule that keeps a deck off a fallen wall is the repair's: 'a repairRaised of a span beside a station whose stretch is breached or dismantled ... first repairs that stretch by repairWall ... so no deck stands on a fallen wall'. S7's generation row maps a breached draw there to worn only because S7 writes conditions after S6's aqueduct. Nothing covers the creation itself. V06 §3.19 (5)'s founding passes the course 'where the course crosses a standing curtain ... through a wall opening ... or a raised gate ... added as S7 furniture in the commit' (V06 l.2824-2826), whatever the run's condition; so do the history replay's founding at generation and a hand aqueduct drawn across a gap (§7.1). Item 114 decays safe, poor or neglected curtains into breached and dismantled runs (T114-3 runs a neglected CITY over 20 epochs). An aqueduct founded later across such a run gets its crossing station on a fallen support at its first commit: a deck standing on nothing, with the clear-span bound read across a station that does not stand. One builder places the station anyway. Another reads a gap as no 'stretch standing' ((d)'s list names 'a dismantled stretch rebuilt on its line' as laid after) and raises an ordinary pier, which (3) slides out of the wall strip. A third repairs the run first.
issues.required_change: §2.7's support step (3), after '(crossings in order along the deck, each taking the nearest interior station not yet taken, ties to the earlier; one added there where none lies within p / 2)', add: '; where the run under that station is breached or dismantled when the raised way is created - an epoch's founding across a decayed curtain (V06 §3.19 (5)), the history replay's, a hand aqueduct drawn across a gap - the creating commit first repairs that stretch by repairWall in the same batch, in item 114's patch material (the row V06 §3.7.7 (3) draws; on a dismantled stretch the op's bend, V06 §2.8: a new stretch drawn on its line), as a repairRaised beside a fallen stretch does (below), so no deck stands on a fallen wall from its first commit, a hand aqueduct's dry run listing the repair as a fate'. Ends: (1) V06: §3.19 (5)'s 'added as S7 furniture in the commit' adds '- a breached or dismantled run at the crossing first repaired by repairWall in that batch, charged to the fabric cap with the founding (§2.7's support step (3))'. (2) scope: §13.2 T114-3 adds 'an aqueduct founded at an epoch across the decayed ring where the run at its crossing is breached, and on a second run dismantled, and a hand aqueduct drawn across such a run: that run repaired in patch material in the creating batch, the station's support standing, never a deck over a gap at any commit, the hand case's undo restoring the gap'. T-V6-73 and V06 §7's T114 row take the epoch case.

issues.claim: CATALOGUE-GAP (C-wall-raised x C-raised-lock). A regeneration with a held raised way: is the crossing station's raised gate re-derived? R5-02 put two sentences into §2.7's support step (6). One: 'A lock or pin holds the same; at a regeneration a locked, pinned or declared raised way stands before every stage the regeneration runs (§7.2)'. The other, its closing sentence (base l.2618-2623): 'at a regeneration the stretches it re-derives are laid after a held raised way (above) - a re-derived stretch on a crossing station's line takes the station into the line as its support again, so an unchanged regeneration reproduces it'. Take a CITY whose S4 timber viaduct crosses S3's ring at a raised gate (T110-2's own fixture), with the viaduct locked, then a full Regenerate (keep). S3's ring is re-derived as a stretch laid after the viaduct. The closing sentence keeps the station as its support - a viaduct's station's support is 'the raised gate, whose tower carries the deck'. But (d) says such a stretch 'takes no crossing station and makes no gate on the deck', and that 'no gate or tower stands in the under-deck strip - one the wall's law would place there moves to the nearest point clear of it'. §4.8 Gates says 'A stretch laid after a raised way takes no crossing furniture' (l.7674-7675), and counts a raised gate only 'where the arterial's raised way was created across the standing trace'. So one builder reproduces the raised gate and N1. Another moves S3's gate out of the under-deck strip, passes the deck over the ring ungated and changes the ring's gates - an unchanged regeneration that does not reproduce. T110-2 (6) runs only 'a Re-derive from S4', which never re-derives S3's ring, so no bar runs the case.
issues.required_change: §2.7's support step (6), closing paragraph: 'a re-derived stretch on a crossing station's line takes the station into the line as its support again, so an unchanged regeneration reproduces it' -> 'a re-derived stretch on a crossing station's line takes the station into the line as its support again with its crossing furniture - a raised gate (the gate law's site there read as that gate, never moved out of the under-deck strip by (d)) or a wall opening (§4.8 Gates) - so an unchanged regeneration reproduces it, its gates and their count included'. Ends: (1) pipeline: §4.8 Gates's 'A stretch laid after a raised way takes no crossing furniture: it runs on beneath the deck, which passes over it with no gate (§2.7's support step (6) (d))' adds '; a stretch a regeneration re-derives on a held raised way's crossing station keeps that station's furniture (§2.7's support step (6))'. (2) scope: §13.2 T110-2 (6) adds 'and a full Regenerate (keep) of the CITY fixture whose S4 timber viaduct crosses S3's ring at a raised gate, that viaduct locked: S3's ring, its N1 gates - the raised gate among them, on its station - and the station's support reproduced byte-identically'.

issues.claim: CATALOGUE-GAP (C-wall-raised x C-raised-edit x C-raised-history). A raised gate whose deck is gone. §4.8 Gates (base l.7655-7673) makes a raised gate a main gate of the ring: 'a gate whose tower carries the deck, its portal on the raised part only'. §5.3's gate row checks at S7's stage end 'every gate joined to the network and the plaza' and counts roads leaving a stage at its raised gates (l.9257). The deck can go in three ways: a hand delete of the viaduct (§7.1 Delete; V06 §3.19.3); V06 §3.19.2's lapse and strike, which fall a generated viaduct's spans by stretch; and a landfall, which ruins the spans beside a station (T114-3's landfall clause). The stretch's fate is stated: held while the deck stands, then an ordinary run 'from the first epoch after the raised way is removed or the spans on both sides of the station have fallen' (§2.7's support step (3)). The gate's fate is not. §4.8 does not say whether the Gate stays in Enceinte.gates with a portal onto a deck that no longer exists, nor what becomes of its tower. V06 §3.19.3 (6)'s delete fates list only the arch vaults, 'the route's standing course' and the aqueduct's terminal. One builder keeps a gate joined to nothing, failing §5.3's check or counting a road that is gone. Another drops the gate and its tower, leaving a held stretch with no tower. A third turns it into a ground gate. The path is normal: T114-3 already runs 'a neglected, poor CITY ring over 20 epochs with ... a viaduct on a raised gate'. (VM-R5T-02 is the station's support after release; this is the Gate record and the counts.)
issues.required_change: §4.8 Gates, after 'taking its own ground gate by §4.2 S3 (4)'s gate law.', add: 'A raised gate is a gate while its deck stands over its station: in the commit that removes its raised way (a hand delete, or its suppression read at a re-derivation) or ruins or clears a span beside its station (V06 §3.19.2 (3), (4); a landfall), it leaves Enceinte.gates, its tower kept on the trace as a wall Tower of the enceinte standing on the held stretch until that stretch is an ordinary run (§2.7's support step (3)), so §5.3's gate checks and counts read the stage without it; a repairRaised that stands both spans beside the station again restores it as the same gate in that batch, and an undo restores it with the event it undoes.' Ends: (1) model: §2.7's support step (3)'s 'a viaduct's or an elevated road's raised gate, whose tower carries the deck' adds '(a gate only while its deck stands, §4.8 Gates)'. (2) V06: §3.19.3 (6)'s dry-run fates add 'for a viaduct or an elevated road on a raised gate, that gate leaving the ring's gates, its tower standing (§4.8 Gates)'. (3) scope: §13.2 T114-3's neglected-CITY clause adds 'once both spans beside the viaduct's raised gate have fallen, the ring's gates exclude it, its tower standing and §5.3's gate checks passing; and a hand delete of the viaduct: the same in that commit, its undo restoring the gate'.
